title: CNY to USD for a US citizen — verified routes, conditional costs, blank unknowns
answer: The reviewed rules do not impose a tax merely on converting or remitting your own principal. The hard problem is proving the lawful source and using the correct current/capital channel. Commercial FX spread and tariffs can be shown only as conditional arithmetic; personal tax, executable FX and receiving fees remain blank.

findings.title: Do not start with the USD 50,000 slogan
findings.body: For a qualifying overseas individual, documented lawful mainland current-account RMB income follows Article 59 rather than a generic USD 50,000 exit cap. Classification and bank review still control.

findings.title: Capital savings need a real capital route
findings.body: Emigrant transfer, inheritance and actual property/corporate transactions are narrow. A US passport alone does not create an emigrant-transfer entitlement.

findings.title: Current provider tariffs are retrievable, but not all-in
findings.body: BOC personal TT is 0.1% capped at CNY 260 plus CNY 150 international cable; SC electronic OUR components vary by tier. FX execution and receiving charges remain unknown.

findings.title: Closed-loop investment is not US repatriation
findings.body: WMC proceeds return to the mainland remittance account; QDII is a product/custody channel; Stock Connect is a trading link.

findings.title: US reporting can matter more than conversion fees
findings.body: FBAR, Form 8938, Form 3520 and worldwide income rules have separate triggers. The treaty saving clause preserves US citizen taxation.

findings.title: Prohibited shortcuts are not cost options
findings.body: Splitting, underground dealing and the 2026 crypto/RWA notice are excluded. No operational guidance is given.
